reconstruction.scope: Principal exterior of the Palace of Fontainebleau, including the mapped White Horse courtyard ranges/north range, central pavilion and two curved horseshoe stair flights, Gallery of Francis I/Cour de la Fontaine ranges, eastern oval court/chapel and northeast service court ranges. Pale masonry, crossed casements, steep slate roofs/dormers and brick chimneys. Open courtyards and independent buildings remain. No furnished rooms, copied crests/inscriptions/sculpture, flags, gardens, fountain sculpture or peripheral stable/administration buildings.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Photo-led exterior reconstruction from two ordinary pictures and mapped footprints. Most heights are absent; use8..20m working eaves, main front12.5m/central pavilion19m, gallery13.5m, south range11.5m, eastern chapel20m and northern range11.5m. Two northeast part tags5/8m are unqualified; exact eaves/ridges are not surveyed. Medial-ridge hip roofs reconstruct the complex unseen roof junctions; dome-like turrets are omitted where unsupported. Repeated windows/quoins/dormers/chimneys and plain pediments abstract the Renaissance detail. Horseshoe stair flights rise4.9m above the working floor; central lower arched gate1.5m recess and upper landing/door are distinct. Gallery has actual recessed arch bays. No copied ornament/artwork. Five existing256px graphs shared by six roles: stone_limestone_raw for pale walls/trim, slate, brick_flemish, storefront and metal_painted. Skyline preserves court holes and simplifies the lower range heights/footprints within5m; district rounds eaves and flattens portals; street has coarser roof ridges and fewer windows/dormers. The closeup preserves full mapped exterior topology. Ornament, sculpture, art and lettering are abstracted or omitted.
